briefdescription.para: Service-entity controller that adapts EntityController to ServiceControllerBase.

detaileddescription.para: In plain words, this file defines a small "adapter" class for each kind of service entity (clinic, pharmacy, laboratory, radiology center). An adapter is a thin wrapper that passes a request straight through to another class that does the real work — here that class is EntityController. Every job listed below (create, read, update, delete, search and their coroutine versions) simply forwards to the matching method of EntityController<T>. This class adds no behaviour of its own: validation, permission checks, building the database query, turning results into JSON and mapping errors to HTTP status codes all happen in that base.

WHY THIS FILE MATTERS IN THE SERVER: It gives service entities their own interface, separate from appointment entities, so the route registry can pick the right controller family by name. The HTTP layer calls these methods through ServiceControllerBase (using a std::variant), and each call lands here and is handed to EntityController. If this file were missing, there would be no concrete class satisfying the service interface and no way to route a clinic/pharmacy/laboratory/radiology request to the real CRUD+S code.

CONCEPTS TO LEARN (for beginners):
C++20 concepts / requires (compile-time checks on template arguments): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/constraints
Templates (writing one class that works for many types): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/templates
C++20 coroutines (functions that pause and resume with co_await/co_return): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/coroutines
